15:35.sourceText: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρνάβας διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ, διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου.
15:35.targetText: And Paul and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming good news—with many others also—the word of the LORD;

15:36.sourceText: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρνάβαν Παῦλος Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πόλιν πᾶσαν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.
15:36.targetText: and after certain days, Paul said to Barnabas, “Having turned back again, we may look after our brothers, in every city in which we have preached the word of the LORD—how they are.”

groups.note: The actual ἐπιστρέψαντες is one returning participle, rendered Having turned back again; back and again are not two separately printed source adverbs.
The actual ἐπισκεψώμεθα is an aorist subjunctive first-person plural, both tags V-ADS-1P, used for the proposed joint visit and rendered we may look after; it is not a future form.
The actual κατηγγείλαμεν is aorist active indicative, rendered English perfect we have preached; no source perfect form is substituted.
The actual ἔχουσιν is have in the how-they-fare expression, rendered they are; it is not a printed εἰμί being verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual δή is an emphatic exhortative particle, not separately expressed by an English now or indeed. The returning verb itself carries the English back/again return wording.
The article under the English our brothers expression is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly adds ἡμῶν with brothers; N1904 has no corresponding possessive pronoun.

15:37.sourceText: Βαρνάβας δὲ ἐβούλετο συνπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάνην τὸν καλούμενον Μάρκον·
15:37.targetText: And Barnabas resolved to take with [them] John called Mark,

groups.note: The actual ἐβούλετο is the wish/plan verb βούλομαι, imperfect with both tags V-INI-3S, rendered resolved; the pinned TR instead has an aorist deliberating form of βουλεύομαι. The actual N1904 head and imperfect analysis are retained. Primary lexical range: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/boulomai .
The actual συνπαραλαβεῖν is one taking-along-with compound infinitive, rendered to take with; no independent Greek with preposition or companion pronoun is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional καί before John is not separately rendered as also; this additive is also absent from the pinned TR wording.
The article before John and the repeated article introducing called Mark are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed companions after take with; no independent companion pronoun is printed in this verse, and no foreign two-name antecedent group is synthesized.

15:38.sourceText: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ συνπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.
15:38.targetText: and Paul was not thinking it good to take him with them who withdrew from them from Pamphylia, and did not go with them to the work;

groups.note: The actual ἠξίου is the deem-worthy or judge-appropriate verb, rendered was thinking it good; thinking, it, and good are not separate source words.

The actual genitive αὐτῶν is the departing-from companion group. English also resumes those same qualified participants as the intended taking-with companions earlier in this sentence. One actual genitive pronoun owns the first two them occurrences; the final go-with-them has its own distinct actual dative αὐτοῖς identity at12.
The actual μή stands with the taking infinitive; English places this same negative in the matrix was-not-thinking-good frame. No additional matrix οὐ negative is invented.
The actual τοῦτον is the this-person demonstrative, rendered him for the proposed taking object; it is not a source αὐτόν personal pronoun.

15:39.sourceText: ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμός, ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρνάβαν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μάρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον.
15:39.targetText: there came, therefore, a sharp contention, so that they were parted from one another, and Barnabas having taken Mark, sailed to Cyprus,

groups.note: The actual παροξυσμός is one sharp-irritation/contention noun, rendered a sharp contention; sharp is not an independently printed Greek adjective.
The actual accusative αὐτούς is the personal subject of the parting infinitive, recast as English nominative they.
The actual ἐκπλεῦσαι is an aorist active sailing-out infinitive under the result construction, rendered finite sailed in the English coordinated clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 connective is δέ, whereas the pinned TR has the inferential οὖν followed by English therefore; the different connectives remain unpaired.
The articles before Barnabas and Mark are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows pinned TR οὖν where N1904 has δέ.

15:40.sourceText: Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν, παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν·
15:40.targetText: and Paul having chosen Silas, went forth, having been given up to the grace of God by the brothers;

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned N1904 names τοῦ Κυρίου, of the Lord, while the pinned TR has τοῦ θεοῦ, of God. These differing genitive named expressions remain whole source/target witness gaps.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows pinned TR θεοῦ instead of N1904 Κυρίου; no detached of is assigned to an unlike named head.

15:41.sourceText: διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.
15:41.targetText: and he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the assemblies.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Syria is not separately expressed.
